question.text: The point $A$ with coordinates $(7,\ln7)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln{x},$ and the point $A'$ with coordinates $(3.5,\ln7)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln(ax),$ shown above. What is the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
The graph of $y=\ln(ax)$ can be obtained from $y=\ln x$ by a horizontal stretch of scale factor $\dfrac{1}{a}.$

From the diagram, we deduce that under such a transformation, the point $(7,\ln7)$ that lies on $y=\ln x$ becomes

\[ \left(\dfrac{1}{a} \cdot 7,\ln 7 \right)=\left(3.5, \ln 7\right) \]

which lies on $y=\ln ax.$

Therefore, $a=2.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=3\log_4(x) +2?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y=3\log_4\left(x\right)+2,$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=\log_4(x).$

  • Stretch it by a scale factor of $3$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=3\log_4(x).$

  • Then, translate the result by $2$ units up to get the graph of $y=3\log_4(x)+2.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=4\ln(x) - 3?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y=4\ln(x) -3,$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y= \ln(x).$

  • Stretch it by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=4\ln(x).$

  • Then, translate the result by $3$ units down to get the graph of $y=4\ln(x) - 3.$
